arxiv-2009-02411.creator: Lin Fu ✉ {}^{\textrm{{\char 0\relax}}}, Sanjeeb Bose, Parviz Moin
arxiv-2009-02411.description: Abstract Accurate prediction of aerothermal surface loading is of paramount importance for the design of high speed flight vehicles. In this work, we consider the numerical solution of hypersonic flow over a double-finned geometry, representative of the inlet of an air-breathing flight vehicle, characterized by three-dimensional intersecting shock-wave/turbulent boundary-layer interaction at Mach 8.3.

arxiv-2205-03829.title: Riemannian Geometry of Optimal Driving and Thermodynamic Length and its Application to Chemical Reaction Networks
arxiv-2205-03829.creator: Dimitri Loutchko, Yuki Sughiyama, Tetsuya J. Kobayashi
arxiv-2205-03829.description: Abstract It is known that the trajectory of an endoreversibly driven system with minimal dissipation is a geodesic on the equilibrium state space. Thereby, the state space is equipped with the Riemannian metric given by the Hessian of the free energy function, known as Fisher information metric.

arxiv-2209-13158.title: Blazar jets as possible sources of ultra-high energy photons: a short review
arxiv-2209-13158.creator: Gopal Bhatta 0000-0002-0705-6619
arxiv-2209-13158.description: Abstract In this work, I present a qualitative discussion on the prospect of production of ultra-high photons in blazars. The sources are a subclass of active galactic nuclei which host supermassive black holes and fire relativistic jets into the intergalactic medium.

arxiv-2308-13473.title: Unlocking the Performance of Proximity Sensors by Utilizing Transient Histograms
arxiv-2308-13473.creator: Carter Sifferman, Yeping Wang, Mohit Gupta, Michael Gleicher
arxiv-2308-13473.description: Abstract We provide methods which recover planar scene geometry by utilizing the transient histograms captured by a class of close-range time-of-flight (ToF) distance sensor. A transient histogram is a one dimensional temporal waveform which encodes the arrival time of photons incident on the ToF sensor.

arxiv-2310-06047.description: Abstract Unsupervised deep learning techniques are widely used to identify anomalous behaviour. The performance of such methods is a product of the amount of training data and the model size. However, the size is often a limiting factor for the deployment on resource-constrained devices.

arxiv-2507-14103.title: Maximal translation surfaces in Lorentz-Minkowski space
arxiv-2507-14103.creator: Rafael López
arxiv-2507-14103.description: Abstract . A translation surface in Lorentz-Minkowski space 𝕃 3 \mathbb{L}^{3} is a surface defined as the sum of two spatial curves. In this paper we present a classification of maximal surfaces of translation type. We prove that if a generating curve is planar, then the other generating curve is also planar. We give a full description of these surfaces.

pmc-10649022.title: Review of Eukaryote Cellular Membrane Lipid Composition, with Special Attention to the Fatty Acids
pmc-10649022.creator: Omeralfaroug Ali, András Szabó, Paramjit S Tappia, Bram Ramjiawan
pmc-10649022.description: Biological membranes, primarily composed of lipids, envelop each living cell. The intricate composition and organization of membrane lipids, including the variety of fatty acids they encompass, serve a dynamic role in sustaining cellular structural integrity and functionality. Typically, modifications in lipid composition coincide with consequential alterations in universally significant signaling pathways.

pmc-11358417.title: Modelling variability and heterogeneity of EMT scenarios highlights nuclear positioning and protrusions as main drivers of extrusion
pmc-11358417.creator: Steffen Plunder, Cathy Danesin, Bruno Glise, Marina A. Ferreira, Sara Merino-Aceituno, Eric Theveneau
pmc-11358417.description: Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) is a key process in physiological and pathological settings. EMT is often presented as a linear sequence with (i) disassembly of cell-cell junctions, (ii) loss of epithelial polarity and (iii) reorganization of the cytoskeleton leading to basal extrusion from the epithelium. Once out, cells can adopt a migratory phenotype with a front-rear polarity.

pmc-11478186.title: Evaluation of the Effect of Topical Prostaglandin Analog Treatment on Orbital Structures in Open-Angle Glaucoma with Computed Tomography
pmc-11478186.creator: Berire Şeyma Durmuş Ece, Zübeyir Yozgat, Hüseyin Bayramlı, Bunyamin Ece, Sonay Aydin, Eun Ji Lee, Manuele Michelessi
pmc-11478186.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: This study aims to evaluate the computed tomography (CT) scans of glaucoma patients using prostaglandin analogs (PGA) in one eye, investigate findings associated with prostaglandin-associated periorbitopathy (PAP), and compare these findings with those of the contralateral eyes. Methods: Patients with open-angle glaucoma who had CT images of the orbital region taken for another reason at least one month after starting PGA treatment in one eye were included in the study.

pmc-11484084.title: MakC and MakD are two proteins associated with a tripartite toxin of Vibrio cholerae
pmc-11484084.creator: Nandita Bodra, Eric Toh, Aftab Nadeem, Sun Nyunt Wai, Karina Persson
pmc-11484084.description: Pathogenic serotypes of Vibrio cholerae, transmitted through contaminated water and food, are responsible for outbreaks of cholera, an acute diarrheal disease. While the cholera toxin is the primary virulence factor, V. cholerae also expresses other virulence factors, such as the tripartite toxin MakABE that is secreted via the bacterial flagellum.

pmc-12804924.title: Computational insights into a protease inhibitor from Streptomyces globosus VITSMAB-2 molecular docking and dynamics simulations against SARS-CoV-2 main protease
pmc-12804924.creator: Shatakshi Mishra, Stany Bala Kumar, Aparana Kumari, K V Bhaskara Rao
pmc-12804924.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Viral proteases are critical components in the life cycles of many dangerous viruses, playing a direct role in facilitating viral replication. Targeting these enzymes through inhibition offers a promising strategy for advancing antiviral agents. This study explores the potential of pigmented actinomycetes from high-altitude terrestrial environments as sources of antiviral agents against SARS-CoV-2, with a particular focus on identifying protease inhibitors.

pmc-13173779.title: Implementing measurement-based care in virtual mental health services for rural veterans: provider insights from a pre-implementation evaluation
pmc-13173779.creator: Amanda Heeren, Kimberly McCoy, Lindsey Fuhrmeister, Natalie Suiter, Jan A Lindsay, Chloe Hoang, Laura Marsh, John Fortney, Carolyn Turvey
pmc-13173779.description: BackgroundMeasurement-Based Care (MBC) uses repeated standardized psychological assessments to monitor treatment progress and guide clinical decision-making. Although MBC improves outcomes when results are discussed collaboratively, adoption across the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) remains below 50%, particularly in virtual and rural settings. This pre-implementation evaluation explored provider perspectives to inform development of a digital MBC workflow for rural tele-mental health settings.

pmc-13291943.title: 3‑Methylthiopropionic Acid Kills Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae by Disrupting Membrane Integrity and Bioenergetics
pmc-13291943.creator: Lirui Ge, Liang Zhao, Saiwa Liu, Jingjing Du, Jian Xu, Kexin Cui, Yu Ga, Jingyu Liu, Dongmei Zhao, Shuwen Wang, Xiaowei Li, Xi Xia
pmc-13291943.description: The rapid dissemination of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM) genes, such as bla NDM‑1 and bla NDM‑5, has rendered carbapenems ineffective against Klebsiella pneumoniae, posing a severe public health threat. Here, we employ comparative metabolomics to reveal that NDM-mediated resistance is underpinned by profound metabolic reprogramming.

pmc-13574864.title: Laser auriculotherapy for the treatment of pain: a scoping review
pmc-13574864.creator: Filipe José Pereira Magalhães, Jéssica Pinheiro Carnaúba, Odaleia de Oliveira Farias, Bernardo Diniz Coutinho, Marli Teresinha Gimeniz Galvão, Mariana Lima Vale
pmc-13574864.description: Purpose: While auriculotherapy is utilized for pain management, the specific application of photobiomodulation (PBM) within this modality remains poorly characterized. This scoping review aims to map the available evidence on PBM in auriculotherapy for pain relief, specifically characterizing therapeutic protocols and laser parameters to guide future research.
